scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Ekikibi originated among the Bakonzo, a Bantu ethnic community inhabiting the Rwenzori mountain range spanning western Uganda and eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, predominantly across Kasese, Bundibugyo, Bunyangabu, and Ntoroko districts.
The dance was conceived through the close observation and admiration of fish swimming in mountain streams, translating aquatic locomotion into human choreography.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Staged principally during weddings and communal festive gatherings, Ekikibi celebrates love, marriage, and domestic happiness.
It articulates harmony and mutual respect between bride and groom as well as their respective families.
In addition to social celebration, the dance honors ancestors and deities, invoking their blessings and spiritual protection over the newly forged marital union.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed by an ensemble usually consisting of four men and four women arrayed in concentric circles, with the men charting an outer path and women holding the inner ring.
Performers execute rhythmic steps, vertical jumps, twists, and complete turns designed to mimic the agile motion of fish in water.
As the concentric formations rotate, the dancers continuously exchange focused eye contact and expressive hand gestures to convey emotional intimacy, affection, and mutual joy.
Watch for Fish mimicry twist, Concentric jump turn.

Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Concentric rings with four men along the outer perimeter and four women within the inner perimeter.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Ekikibi is accompanied by vocal love songs specifically composed to praise the character and union of the bride and groom.
The instrumental backing is anchored by drums providing percussive cadence, supplemented by rattles for sharp rhythmic texture and flutes carrying melodic phrases.
Listen for the drums, flutes, rattles.

The sonic texture is characterized by driving drum patterns intertwined with continuous shaken rattle pulses and melodic flute interludes. Over this percussive tapestry, vocalists deliver celebratory love songs dedicated to the couple, creating a bright, uplifting atmosphere appropriate for marital rites.
